grades.quote: Often this means that at least some of the distributed file system software is part of the operating system kernel itself, contrary to the norm for application-layer protocols.
grades.reason: Says distributed file systems must be visible through the OS's normal file-system support, so part of the software is often in the kernel. It doesn't say where or how the kernel dispatches an open to the network filesystem (for example a VFS layer), so it is only background.
Lists networking programming projects (threaded server, HTTP client, socket addresses). It says nothing about kernel dispatch of file operations to a network filesystem.

Lists exploration exercises on DNS, NFS and CIFS. It mentions NFS lookup versus open only in an exercise prompt and does not explain how the kernel dispatches a file operation to the network filesystem.
Covers DNS resource records, the resolver and the name-server protocol. It does not cover file operations or network filesystem dispatch in the kernel.
